correctness.rationale: The exact metric quotient relation is min(delta(x-y),delta(x+y)); the surjective Haar group endomorphism makes these distances iid. Nearest-lattice orthotope reduction is exact. The centered ball–orthotope volume is a log-concave marginal in log halfwidths by Prékopa, hence symmetric Schur-concave; strict Karamata comparison of the orthotope circumradius yields strict stochastic ordering for nonpermutations. Circular segments give the 2D CDF; local simplex scaling proves the doubled terminal-tail exponent. Independent CDF simulation and deterministic quadrature checks pass (2,241 thresholds; four 150,000-pair samples). Analytic proof, not finite tests, covers all d>=2.

value.rationale: Two-point intrinsic geodesic distance is a meaningful metric-measure observable. The theorem completely orders every pair of equal-volume orthogonal inversion quotient shapes whose log lengths are comparable by majorization, establishes a unique cubic optimum simultaneously for all increasing costs, and gives exact CDF, short-distance correction, and doubled diameter-tail exponents. This is stronger than computing a single routine moment and distinguishes a singular quotient from the covering torus while explicitly limiting scope to orthogonal lattices.
